Definition: from G2095 and G4576; well-reverent, i.e. pious:--devout, godly.
BiblicalUsage: eusebḗs is a plain word for devout, godly. In Acts 10:2, the text says "A] devout [man." In Acts 10:7, the text says "and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually."
TheologicalSignificance: I take eusebḗs to mean that faithfulness is staying when staying is costly — the way God stays with us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
